originalTitle: Michael Burry Says His Portfolio Was Discussed 'About the Time the Market Reversed Off Its Lows': He Is 'Temporarily Almost Entirely Long'
summary: Michael Burry‘s move to a portfolio that is almost entirely long was discussed on financial news just as U.S. stocks reversed off their lows on Wednesday, the ‘Big Short’ investor noted. Timing Of His Portfolio Review Burry told subscribers of his Substack, ‘Cassandra Unchained,’ earlier Wednesday that his portfolio is more long and less short than it has been in some time. “My portfolio review was discussed on CNBC about the time the market reversed off its lows today,” he said in a post on X.
content:
Michael Burry 's move to a portfolio that is almost entirely long was discussed on financial news just as U.S. stocks reversed off their lows on Wednesday, the 'Big Short' investor noted.

"My portfolio review was discussed on CNBC about the time the market reversed off its lows today," he said in a post on X.

My portfolio review was discussed on CNBC about the time the market reversed off its lows today. https://t.co/n0aYgNBXPl

— Cassandra Unchained (@michaeljburry) November 25, 2026

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged more than 1,100 points to a low on Wednesday before reversing to close 0.33% higher at 50,182.95.

The Nasdaq Composite, down 4.6% at its low, finished 0.62% lower at 23,585.80, while the S&P 500, down 3.2% at its low, ended 0.25% lower at 7,182.78.

Read Also: Nvidia Put on Negative Credit Watch by S&P Over 'Key Man' Risk: Moody's Says Jensen Huang's Return as CEO 'Reduces Near-Term Uncertainty'

Aside from puts on Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) and MetLife Inc. (NYSE:MET) , Burry said he is "temporarily almost entirely long," putting gains into stocks he considers undervalued.

He sold the final half of his Nasdaq 100 put position on a weak day for tech and holds roughly 25% of his portfolio in cash.

With volatility elevated, he said puts on even staid companies loosely tied to the AI buildout cost too much right now.

He plans to bet against Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) again near $200 a share once optimism returns.

How AI-Linked Stocks Moved Wednesday

AI-related stocks were lower Wednesday, with Nvidia dropping 3.91%, while Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) fell 4.5%, Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) declined more than 5.11%, and Alphabet Inc. 's Class A (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Class C (NASDAQ:GOOG) stock fell more than 2%.

The stocks traded higher in after-hours action, with Nvidia up 1.29%, Micron rose 2.34%, and Oracle up 1.89%, while Alphabet's Class C and Class A shares gained 0.67% and 0.69%, respectively.

Price Action: The State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) closed 0.29% lower on Wednesday at $716.70 and was up 0.52% in extended trading, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) fell 0.65% to close at $633.93 and rose 0.42% in after-hours trading.

Benzinga Edge rankings indicate the Invesco QQQ Trust has a Momentum score in the 39th percentile, with a negative price trend across the short, medium, and long term.
